verdicts.tldr: CheckTx decodes the tx outside any recover, so a future amino decode panic escapes BaseApp on the mempool path instead of returning ErrTxDecode
verdicts.details: Head CheckTx calls amino.Unmarshal(req.Tx, &tx) at baseapp.go:645 before runTxWithDecoded, whose recover is the defer at :884. At the merge base CheckTx went straight to runTx, where the recover defer (base :828) precedes the only decode (base :897). No input panics the decoder today, so this is latent: the user loses only a safety net that #5399 showed was needed. Fix: wrap the CheckTx decode in a defer/recover that returns ErrTxDecode, or move it after a recover.
verdicts.evidence: Read only. head baseapp.go:645 `if err := amino.Unmarshal(req.Tx, &tx); err != nil {` precedes :884 `defer func() { if r := recover()`; base baseapp.go:638-640 CheckTx -> runTx, recover at :828, `amino.Unmarshal(txBytes, &tx)` at :897.
verdicts.verify_by: Re-introduce a decode panic (for example, restore the panic in amino typeURLtoFullname that 8b8e1f8e7 removed) and run `go test -count=1 -run TestCheckTxMalformedTypeURL ./tm2/pkg/sdk/` in head and at the merge base: head panics and base returns !IsOK. The fix wraps the CheckTx decode in a recover returning ErrTxDecode.

verdicts.tldr: Each admitted sponsored tx reserves the full credit window in block packing even when PayGas capped it lower; documented tradeoff, and the proposed min() fix is not a sound bound
verdicts.details: ante.go:399-403 reports MaxGasCreditPerTx as GasWanted for a 0-fee tx, runTx copies it (baseapp.go:995, :1056), and ReapMaxBytesMaxGas sums memTx.gasWanted against maxGas (clist_mempool.go:498-500), so at most MaxGas/window sponsored txs fit per block. The code comment states this is deliberate, to bound packing by worst-case use. The finder's fix, min(credit, meter limit after CheckExecute), is not an upper bound for DeliverTx, which may take another path and call PayGas with a larger maxFee against different state. Fix: leave as is unless DeliverTx enforces the CheckExecute limit; at most mention the throughput cost in the ADR.
verdicts.evidence: Read only. ante.go:397-401 `reportedGasWanted = consParams.Block.MaxGasCreditPerTx` with comment 'keeps block packing bounded by real worst-case consumption'; paygas.go:54-61 `m.GasMeter.SetLimit(limit)` lowers only the meter; clist_mempool.go:498 `newTotalGas := totalGas + memTx.gasWanted`.
verdicts.verify_by: Read the code. A unit test in which the handler of a sponsored CheckTx calls ctx.GasMeter().SetLimit(3_000_000) shows res.GasWanted == MaxGasCreditPerTx. The fix reports min(credit, ctx.GasMeter().Limit()) from CheckExecute.

verdicts.tldr: payGas/payStorage rows charge about 415 gas more than measured at the shortest path, because the base is floored to the N=12 sample and the slope then charges those 12 bytes again
verdicts.details: fit_linear sets base = max(intercept, ns[0]) (line 439), and the bench at N=12 reads 1097 ns, the ADR's base. nativeSizeOf charges the full tv.GetLength() (native_gas.go:357), so a 12-byte path costs 1097 + 35448*12/1024 = 1512 gas against 1097 measured. The floor predates the diff (base line 433) and prices other LenString rows the same way; the new rows inherit it, and the body already notes the rows need re-measuring. Fix: floor to ns[0] - slope*sizes[0] for these rows, or accept the conservative bias.
verdicts.evidence: Read only. gen_native_table.py:439 `base = max(float(coeffs[0]), float(ns[0]))`; sponsorship_bench_m1pro_arm64.txt `BenchmarkNative_Runtime_PayGas_12-10 218295 1097 ns/op`; ADR line 88 `payGas charges 1097 + 35448·len(pkgPath)/1024`.
verdicts.verify_by: python3 gen_native_table.py sponsorship_bench_m1pro_arm64.txt --no-plot --md-out /dev/null --go-out /dev/null prints Base 1097 = ns at N=12 (fit_linear: base = max(coeffs[0], ns[0])); nativeSizeOf at gnovm/pkg/gnolang/native_gas.go:357 charges the full tv.GetLength(). Fix: floor to ns[0] - slope*sizes[0]

verdicts.tldr: The use-case test the ADR cites for the ~6M window floor only asserts admission at 30M, so a cost rise past 6M stays green
verdicts.details: The only check is require.True(res.IsOK()) at a 30M window, then a t.Logf of gasUsed. The ADR (line 87) cites this test for 'about 6M gas ... the credit window must be at least that'. An operator sizing the window from the ADR gets no signal when the cost grows. Fix: assert res.GasUsed under a stated bound for the GRC20 approve+transferFrom case, or run it at the window the ADR names.
verdicts.evidence: Read only. sponsorship_usecase_test.go:315 `require.True(t, res.IsOK(), "should be admitted at a 30M window: ...")` and :316 `t.Logf(... gasUsed ...)`, no other assertion on res.GasUsed; ADR:87 'uses about 6M gas (`sponsorship_usecase_test.go`)'.
verdicts.verify_by: go test -count=1 -v -run TestSponsorshipUseCaseFitsWindow ./gno.land/pkg/gnoland/ and read the gasUsed log lines; grep -n 'require' around line 315 shows no bound on res.GasUsed

verdicts.tldr: user1's balance is captured and re-queried but never compared, so the test cannot see who paid user1's share
verdicts.details: Line 28 copies stdout to user1_balance_before, which nothing reads, and the final query at line 44 has no stdout or cmp after it. The comment above says user1 pays counter.Increment's storage; if the payer realm paid it, or user1 paid gas, the fixture stays green. Fix: compare the final balance against user1_balance_before (expect a drop by the storage deposit only), or drop both queries.
verdicts.evidence: Read only. txtar lines 27-28 `gnokey query bank/balances/$user1_user_addr` / `cp stdout user1_balance_before`; lines 42-44 comment then `gnokey query bank/balances/$user1_user_addr` followed by the `-- counter/gnomod.toml --` section with no check.
verdicts.verify_by: Read lines 27-44: no `cmp` or `stdout` follows the final `gnokey query bank/balances/$user1_user_addr`, and user1_balance_before has no reader.

verdicts.tldr: The 'cost comparison' fixture prints three gas figures and relates none of them, so a PayGas overhead regression passes
verdicts.details: Each of the three calls asserts only `stdout OK!` and `stdout 'GAS USED:   \d+'`; the closing comment describes the difference between call 2 and call 3 but nothing measures it. Fix: capture the figures and assert the PayGas call's overhead stays under a bound, or rename it as a smoke test.
verdicts.evidence: Read only. txtar CALL 1/2/3 blocks each end with `stdout OK!` and `stdout 'GAS USED:   \d+'`; trailing comment '## Difference in GAS USED = PayGas + PayStorage + cross-realm call overhead.' with no assertion.
verdicts.verify_by: Read lines 19-35: the only checks are `stdout OK!` and `stdout 'GAS USED:   \d+'`.

verdicts.tldr: A sponsored tx that runs out of gas after PayGas gets a log naming the 10M credit window as its gas wanted, not the ~3M PayGas cap that stopped it
verdicts.details: For a 0-fee tx the ante reports MaxGasCreditPerTx (ante.go:401), runTx stores it in gasWanted (baseapp.go:995), and the OOG branch passes that to OutOfGasLog (:901), which prints 'exceeds tx's gas wanted (%d) ... simulate with consensus maximum'. PayGas lowered only the meter (paygas.go:61 SetLimit), so the user reads a used figure below the stated wanted figure. ante.go:140/143 likewise logs and reports tx.Fee.GasWanted for a 0-fee tx, unlike the success path. Fix: pass ctx.GasMeter().Limit() at baseapp.go:901 and newCtx.GasMeter().Limit() at ante.go:140/143.
verdicts.evidence: Read only, the fixture not run. ante.go:401 `reportedGasWanted = consParams.Block.MaxGasCreditPerTx`; baseapp.go:995 `gasWanted = result.GasWanted`; :901 `store.OutOfGasLog(gasUsed, gasWanted, maxGas, ex.Descriptor, true)`; gas.go:141 'gas used (%d) exceeds tx's gas wanted (%d) ...'; testscript_gnoland.go:293 `bp.MaxGasCreditPerTx = 10_000_000`; ante.go:140 `OutOfGasLog(gasUsed, tx.Fee.GasWanted, ...)`. Running paygas_oog_after_paygas with the added stderr line would confirm the printed figure.
verdicts.verify_by: Add `stderr 'exceeds tx.s gas wanted \(10000000\)'` after line 23 of gno.land/pkg/integration/testdata/paygas_oog_after_paygas.txtar and run `go test -count=1 -p 1 -parallel 1 ./gno.land/pkg/integration/ -run 'TestTestdata/paygas_oog_after_paygas$'`: it passes, which shows the 10M figure. The fix passes ctx.GasMeter().Limit() (basicGasMeter.Limit, gas.go:199) at baseapp.go:901 and newCtx.GasMeter().Limit() at ante.go:140/143.
